title: Dashboards debt + cost scrub — sprint handoff notes
content:
Purpose
---
Weekly handoff note covering the observability team’s sprint work on trace retention, dashboard debt, and our cost-scrub playbook. This is written as an operational summary + standup log for the on-call and for partners (platform, runtime, and finance) to pick up where we left off.

High-level summary
---
- Focus this sprint: reduce cardinality and surface cheap-but-actionable dashboards; finish the first iteration of throttled full-trace retention for low-value tenants; and validate cost impact of new sampling changes.
- Outcome: prototype sampling + TTL policy merged to staging (PR 879), three dashboards marked for removal or merge, and a 12% drop in monthly trace storage estimate from our cost model.
- Open risks: unknown QoE impact for a small set of latency regressions (see Blockers). Need an A/B on sampling logic next week.

Key metrics (observed during sprint)
---
- Avg traces/day (cluster): 42M (down from 48M pre-scrub)
- 99p latency (trace capture pipeline): 2.1s (target <2s for ingestion to index)
- Estimated monthly trace storage (projected): $23k -> $20.2k (approx -12%)
- Dashboard queries flagged as heavy: 18 queries (top 5 consume ~60% of dashboard read QPS)
- Sampling efficiency: retained ~6% of traces for long-tail error-case testing, but captured ~86% of high-latency (>2s) traces in preliminary sample run

Standup snippets (Mon -> Wed)
---
Mon 2026-04-27 — Kickoff + scope
- Lucas: finished telemetry delta for storage model (sheet attached in Confluence). Confirmed primary cost drivers: high-cardinality tags (user_id/session_id), long retention policies for dev/test tenants.
- Priya: started a dashboard inventory pass; found ~27 dashboards that are duplicates or editor copies. Began marking merge candidates in the dashboard repo.
- Maya: sketched TTL policy for traces by tenant tier; pushed initial config to staging (experimental).

Tue 2026-04-28 — Prototype testing
- Jonas: landed PR for sampling filter (retains all traces with error OR duration>1200ms; otherwise applies probabilistic sampling). Scoped as feature-flagged.
- Aisha: smoke-tested PR 879 against the staging ingest pipeline; observed ingestion latency spike when full-trace writes hit a specific storage node (investigating with infra).
- Action: reduce dashboard auto-refresh on heavy queries to 1/6th frequency during business hours (temporary) — assigned to Priya.

Wed 2026-04-29 — Cost scrub session + ops drills
- Finance joined: reviewed projected savings and asked for a 30/60/90 day runway plan with conservative + optimistic projections.
- Emergent item: two internal teams (SDK and Console) rely on intensive dashboard queries that assume un-sampled data. Need to communicate expected blindspots and provide temporary export jobs for historical analysis.
- Decision: sampling will be on by default for dev/test tenants next week; prod tenants will be opt-in for the A/B until we have a fidelity report.

Action items (owners & deadlines)
---
- Priya: merge dashboard duplicates and reduce heavy queries refresh frequency; PR/cleanup by 2026-05-03. (JIRA-OBS-4131)
- Lucas: finalize conservative vs optimistic cost model and provide 30/60/90 day projection for Finance by 2026-05-01. Attach: cost-model-sheet in Confluence.
- Jonas: add telemetry hook to record which traces get sampled/dropped (for fidelity comparisons). Deliverable: instrumentation + dashboard by 2026-05-06. (JIRA-OBS-4140)
- Aisha: continue infra investigation for ingestion latency spikes; coordinate with infra on port-level throttling test and report back by 2026-04-30. (Slack thread #obs-ingest-spikes)
- Maya: draft partner communication for Console & SDK teams describing sampling implications and a temporary query-export workaround. Send by 2026-04-30.

Blockers & open questions
---
1) Ingestion spike root cause: specific storage node became hot when a bulk historical export job ran concurrently with a retention compaction. Infra needs to validate whether compaction scheduling can be moved to off-peak windows without impacting other tenants. (blocking Aisha’s work)
2) Fidelity: Do we have adequate coverage to assert that probabilistic sampling + heuristic retention doesn’t miss signal for regression detection? Need targeted A/B analysis on 10 recent incidents. (owner: Jonas)
3) Dashboard owners: Several dashboards have no owner metadata. We need a policy-enforced owner field for every dashboard to avoid accidental deletions. (owner: Priya/product)
4) Cost allocation: Finance asked whether we can attribute trace storage costs back to product teams automatically. Short-term answer: no automatic attribution — we will provide weekly CSV exports and proposed tagging for next quarter.

Decisions taken this sprint
---
- Enable probabilistic sampling behind a feature flag for dev/test tenants next week; prod tenants remain unchanged until fidelity checks pass.
- Merge or archive duplicate dashboards rather than creating new variants; heavy queries to be rewritten as pre-aggregates where possible.
- Introduce a mandatory dashboard owner field in the dashboard template; dashboard creation form will enforce this starting next sprint.

Runbook/Playbook snippets (draft)
---
- Cheap heartbeats: if dashboard QPS > 1000/min and average runtime > 800ms, apply a read-cache TTL of 60s and mark for rewrite.
- Sampling toggle quick-revert:
  - To disable sampling globally: feature-flag off in obs-config -> reload ingest config (api: /api/v1/config/reload) -> watch ingestion 99p latency for 10m.
  - To enable sampling fallback: set sample_rate_override to 1.0 for prod tenant in console (temp) and re-sync.

Communication & stakeholders
---
- FYI list: Platform Eng (platform-engineering@redwood.ai), Runtime (serving-runtime@redwood.ai), Console PM (Nate Kim), Finance (Elena Morales).
- Required: Console & SDK teams to test analytics export flow by 2026-05-05.

Notes to follow-up with next week
---
- Run the A/B fidelity run across 10 incidents and produce a short fidelity report (Jonas).
- Confirm ingestion compaction reschedule plan (Infra).
- Implement dashboard owner enforcement and a small training for product teams on how to flag heavy queries (Priya + Product Ops).

Appendix: quick queries and pointers
---
- Heavy trace query example (for dashboard rewrite): SELECT count(*) FROM traces WHERE service = 'ingest' AND tags['operation'] = 'write' AND timestamp > now() - interval '1h';
- Staging PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/879
- Confluence: Dashboard Cleanup Q2 2026 (linked above).

If you pick this up while I'm OOO tomorrow: start with the Aisha infra ticket (logs under slack #obs-ingest-spikes) and prioritize the fidelity A/B. — Maya
